tasks.short: Order print library materials, check prices and costs, prepare slips, and pay.

steps.what: Talk with the librarian about which materials to order.
Open a title request for the library materials.
Read supplier prices for the print order.
Record quoted prices and quantities on the request.
Compute order costs from the stored prices.
Assemble draft order slips from stored fields.
Check prices and costs against the supplier quote.
Send the accepted order slips to the supplier.
Release payments for the accepted library order.

tasks.design: The technician writes the supplier unit price onto the title request in {OTHER}. {OTHER} then totals quantity times that stored price and assembles draft order slips from those fields. The technician checks the prices and costs against the quote. Only after that check does the technician send the accepted slips by {EMAIL} and release the payment in {ERP}. Neither release edits the accepted order. The librarian still chooses the titles.
tasks.previous_blocker: The unit price lived in a supplier quote the acquisitions module did not total, so each cost was figured by hand before the slip and the payment.
tasks.enabler_now: {OTHER} can store a unit price and a quantity on the request and total them. The send and the payment stay separate releases of one accepted order.
tasks.still_hard: A quote with no unit price, a fund the librarian has not named, and a supplier note that changes the edition still need the technician.
tasks.human_edge: The technician judges whether the quoted price and edition are the ones the librarian asked for, and releases the money.
tasks.altitude: Less time retyping prices into slips. The same time on the librarian conversation, the quote, the send, and the payment. No new right to choose titles or to pay.

reach.task: Choose which titles and editions to buy
reach.learn: The technician records only the title the librarian named, and does not send an order the librarian has not chosen.

evidence.claim: An acquisitions module can store a supplier unit price, a fund, and a title, total quantity times that price, and hold draft order slips for a person to send and pay.
Basic company administration is kept for 7 years, so the order and the payment record of this library stay available for an audit.
Works-council consent is needed if the system logs and checks the technician's order work.

assumptions: The prior's price tally, about ten points, is counted with the document steps and kept as stored fields in {OTHER}.
The technician stores the unit price in a4 before the cost total runs. If the quote has no unit price, a5 and a6 do not run.
a5 and a6 are drafts. They do not wait for a later check. a7 reads them and names accepted library order v1 without editing them. a8 and a9 release that version and do not edit it.
A mismatch sends the technician back to a4. It does not change the slips inside a7.
No extra focal hours. Quote exceptions stay inside a7 and a4.
The payment is irreversible, so the gate sits on a9, not on the cost total.
unknowns: Whether every supplier quote states a unit price the technician can store.
Whether this library's orders are company administration covered by the 7-year rule, or a public body under other record law.
Whether the works council must consent before an accept or reject log on orders goes live.
research_questions: What share of title requests arrives with a unit price on the supplier quote?
Who may release a supplier payment today, the technician or a finance colleague?

already_counted.description: Checking prices and costs against the quote, and naming the accepted order, is the time in a7.

incremental.description: Upkeep of the price-total and slip-assembly rules in the acquisitions module.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is zero when the quote has no unit price, so the cost total and the slips do not run. High counts only the cost total, and only when every line has a stored unit price. Supplier notes stay in the check. The net also includes slip assembly.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Send notices about lost or overdue books.

steps.what: Open the loan for the overdue books.
Read the due date and the lost mark.
Read the stored wording used for notices.
Draft overdue notices from stored loan fields.
Check notices name the right books and patron.
Send the accepted overdue notices to the patron.
Record the notice date on the loan.
Talk with the patron about a disputed book.

tasks.design: For a loan already open in {OTHER}, the system drafts an overdue or lost notice from the stored due date, title, and patron address, using wording this task does not write. The technician checks that the notice names the right books and patron and names accepted overdue notice v1. {OTHER} then sends that version by {EMAIL} and writes the notice date on the loan. The send and the date write do not change the wording. A dispute with the patron stays a conversation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each notice was addressed by hand because the due date, the title, and the patron address were not assembled into one send.
tasks.enabler_now: {OTHER} already holds the loan, the due date, and the patron address, and can send a scheduled notice once those fields are present.
tasks.still_hard: A loan with no due date or no patron address, a lost book the patron disputes, and wording this task does not own.
tasks.human_edge: The technician confirms the notice is about the right books and the right patron before it leaves, and hears a dispute in person.
tasks.altitude: Less time addressing overdue notices. The same time opening the loan, reading the due date, checking the books, and talking with a patron. No new right to waive a fine.

reach.task: Decide whether a lost book is replaced
reach.learn: The notice names the book. The librarian decides replacement. The technician does not decide it in the send.

evidence.claim: A library system can prepare a scheduled overdue notice from a stored due date, patron address, and title, and can send that notice.
Public-interest archiving exemptions do not cover a company library's mail to patrons. Ordinary personal-data rules still apply.
Works-council consent is needed if notice logs are used to check the technician's work.

assumptions: The prior's loan-date tally, about five points, is counted with the document steps and kept on the loan in {OTHER}.
Notice wording already exists on the loan type. This task reads it and does not write it.

b4 drafts the notice and stops when the draft is written. It does not wait for b5. b5 names accepted overdue notice v1 and does not edit the draft. b6 sends that version. b7 writes only the notice date.
If the due date or the patron address is missing, b4 and b6 do not run.
A lost mark already stored on the loan selects the lost wording. The technician does not invent a collection rate.
No extra focal hours. Disputed books stay inside b5 and b8.
Patron mail is personal data. The archiving exemption is not treated as permission to send it.
unknowns: Whether every overdue loan already stores a due date and a patron address.
Whether the works council must consent before a log of notice checks goes live.
Who owns the notice wording today, and how often it changes.
research_questions: What share of loans has both a due date and a patron address stored before this task starts?
Is the patron address already used for circulation mail today?

already_counted.description: Checking that the notice names the right books and patron is the time in b5.

incremental.description: Upkeep of the scheduled notice rule and the stored wording in the circulation module.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is zero when the due date or the patron address is not on the loan. High counts only the send, and only when both are stored and the technician has named the accepted notice. The draft and the date write are in the net. Disputed books stay a conversation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Retrieve central information for storage on the library computer.

steps.what: Read the request to retrieve library information.
Read the identifier on the item in hand.
Confirm the identifier on the library computer.
Retrieve information from central databases into the computer.
Check the retrieved record matches the item in hand.
Commit the accepted copy for library storage.

tasks.design: The technician reads the identifier on the item and confirms that the library computer in {OTHER} already holds it. {OTHER} retrieves the matching bibliographic fields from the central catalogue into a draft copy. If more than one central record matches, it stores nothing. The technician checks the hit against the item and names accepted catalogue copy v1. {OTHER} commits that version for storage and does not edit it.
tasks.previous_blocker: The technician retyped the central record into the library computer, and a second matching record was easy to store by mistake.
tasks.enabler_now: The identifier is already on the item record from accession, and {OTHER} can copy stored bibliographic fields from the central catalogue when exactly one record matches.
tasks.still_hard: An item with no identifier, two central records for one item, and reading the identifier on the item in hand.
tasks.human_edge: The technician decides which central record is the item in hand, and refuses a copy when the match is not single.
tasks.altitude: Less retyping of a single matching record into the library computer. The same time on the item in hand and on choosing between two matches. No new right to discard a record.

reach.task: Choose which edition to keep when two central records match
reach.learn: The technician does not store a copy until one record is accepted. Two matches go to the librarian.

evidence.claim: Stored bibliographic fields can be copied from a central catalogue into the local catalogue when one record matches an identifier the library already holds.
No Annex III area covers copying a catalogue record into a library computer.
Works-council consent is needed if the system logs and checks which catalogue copy the technician accepts.

assumptions: The prior's small tally, about four points, is counted with the document steps.
The identifier is already stored on the item record from accession. c3 confirms it. c3 does not create it. If it is absent, c4 does not run.
c4 retrieves one match and stops. It writes nothing when several central records match, and it does not wait for c5. c5 names accepted catalogue copy v1. c6 commits that version and does not edit it.
This store stays inside the library. It is not a send outside the organisation.
No extra focal hours. Two-match cases stay inside c5.
Reading the identifier on the item is unchanged, so that step stays at full time.
unknowns: Whether accession already stores an identifier on every item this task retrieves.
How often the central catalogue returns two records for one item.
Whether the works council must consent before a log of accepted copies goes live.
research_questions: What share of items already carries an identifier that matches one central record?
Which central catalogue is the source, and is the copy agreement already in place?

already_counted.description: Checking the retrieved record against the item and naming the accepted copy is the time in c5.

incremental.description: Upkeep of the field-copy link between the central catalogue and the library computer.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is zero when the item has no stored identifier or the central catalogue has no single match. High counts only the retrieve, and only for a single match. Choosing between two records stays with the technician. The commit is in the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Verify bibliographical data for author, title, publisher, and edition.

steps.what: Open the bibliographical record for the materials.
Read author, title, publisher, publication date, and edition.
Read the stored author, title, publisher, and edition.
Compare author, title, publisher, publication, and edition.
Check bibliographical matches against the item in hand.
Commit the accepted bibliographical data for the materials.
Read a publisher reply when publication data is missing.

tasks.design: The technician reads author, title, publisher, publication date, and edition on the item. {OTHER} compares those five stored fields with the shared-catalogue record and writes a comparison, not a new description. The technician checks the comparison against the item and names accepted bibliographical data v1, correcting a field when the item disagrees. {OTHER} commits that version and does not choose the edition. A publisher reply is only read when publication data is missing.
tasks.previous_blocker: The five fields were compared by eye, and a disagreement about edition had no separate commit of the version the technician accepted.
tasks.enabler_now: Author, title, publisher, publication date, and edition are stored fields, so code can mark an exact match or a mismatch without a model.
tasks.still_hard: The item in hand, a missing publication date, and any case where the item and the catalogue disagree on edition.
tasks.human_edge: The technician decides the edition when the item and the record disagree, using the item and, when needed, the publisher reply.
tasks.altitude: Less time on an exact field match. The same time reading the item, resolving a mismatch, and reading a publisher reply. No new right to set an edition the item does not support.

reach.task: Confirm an edition when the item and the catalogue disagree
reach.learn: The comparison only marks a mismatch. The librarian confirms the edition the technician cannot settle from the item.

evidence.claim: Code can compare author, title, publisher, publication date, and edition on a stored record with the same fields on a shared-catalogue record.
No Annex III area covers a field comparison of bibliographical data.
Works-council consent is needed if the system logs and checks the technician's bibliographical corrections.

assumptions: The prior's small tally, about three points, is counted with the document steps.

d4 compares stored fields and stops when the comparison is written. It does not wait for d5 and it does not choose an edition. d5 names accepted bibliographical data v1. d6 commits that version and does not edit it.
A mismatch or missing publication data stays with the technician. d7 only reads a reply. It does not send one.
The physical reading of the item is unchanged, so that step stays at full time.
No extra focal hours. Edition disputes stay inside d5 and d2.
This task does not draft a description and does not suggest subject headings.
unknowns: Whether author, title, publisher, publication date, and edition are already stored on every record this task opens.
How often the item and the shared catalogue disagree on edition.
Whether the works council must consent before a log of bibliographical corrections goes live.
research_questions: What share of materials has all five fields stored before the comparison runs?
Who answers a missing publication date today, the publisher or the librarian?

already_counted.description: Checking the five fields against the item and naming the accepted bibliographical data is the time in d5.

incremental.description: Upkeep of the five-field comparison against the shared catalogue.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is zero when the item is not on the shared catalogue or publication data is missing. High counts only the field comparison on a clean match. The item in hand and a publisher reply stay with the technician. The commit is in the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Less retyping of orders, notices, and catalogue copies. The same time on the item in hand, on price judgement, and on talks with librarians and readers. No new decision right.
skills_to_grow: Read a supplier quote into stored price fields before a cost total runs.
Check an overdue notice against the loan and the patron before it is sent.
Confirm the edition in hand when a catalogue field does not match.
role.ambitious_version: The same duties. Less time retyping orders, notices, and catalogue copies. The technician does not gain a new service or a new group to serve.
